answer: PostgreSQL was chosen for billing because auditability mattered more than DynamoDB's lower migration effort. DynamoDB was tried, but the migration failed because conditional-update semantics did not match the existing transaction flow; Claude later confirmed the failure after reviewing integration-test output.
The initial Redis test increased cache invalidation complexity, so it was abandoned. A narrower retry later produced negligible latency improvement.
The first invoice export attempt timed out after 18 minutes. Exports were switched to asynchronous jobs, and the first full customer batch then completed successfully.

The sequence was polling as the temporary compatibility path, then webhooks, then temporarily disabled webhooks because duplicate deliveries caused reconciliation errors, and finally re-enabled webhooks after idempotency handling. The latest state is webhooks re-enabled.
